sources.title: Tajik Soviet Socialist Republic
sources.note: ASSR 14 October 1924 inside the Uzbek SSR; union republic 5 December 1929; Stalinabad 1929, Dushanbe 10 November 1961; sovereignty 24 August 1990; 31 August 1991 renamed; 9 September 1991 independence; area 143,100 km2 (no year).

sources.title: Uzbek Soviet Socialist Republic
sources.note: 15 October 1929: Tajik ASSR and a region around Khujand split off and become the Tajik SSR.

notes: No Cliopatria row; the land lies inside Union of Soviet Socialist Republics shapes (1924-1991); Cliopatria's Republic of Tajikistan begins in 1992. The republic is an internal unit of the Soviet Union (an autonomous republic of the Uzbek SSR until 1929, recorded there as a vassal). Dates: the Uzbek page puts the split at 15 October 1929, the Tajik page at December 1929 (the gain uses October, the rename December). The page is silent on Khujand by name, on Leninabad, on the Gorno-Badakhshan oblast, and on the year of the 143,100 km2. The Tajik ASSR's lands are Tajikistan without the Khujand region (Natural Earth Leninabad); the Bukharan dossier gives East Bukhara as Khatlon, Dushanbe and Gorno-Badakhshan, which leaves the Rasht lands (Natural Earth "Tadzhikistan Territories") undecided. Counterparts: the Uzbek SSR and bukharan-people-s-soviet-republic dossiers exist.
